I checked this by case analysis on a few triangles, and the graph is **not** 3-colorable.

**Key triangle:** nodes 0, 1, 9 are mutually adjacent, so they use three distinct colors. Without loss of generality, 0 = R, 1 = G, 9 = B.

**Case 1: 7 = R.** Node 7 is adjacent to 1, so this is allowed.
- 25 is adjacent to 1 (G) and 7 (R), so 25 = B.
- 23 is adjacent to 7 (R) and 25 (B), so 23 = G.
- 27 is adjacent to 0 (R), 7 (R), and 23 (G), so 27 = B.
- 3 is adjacent to 0 (R) and 23 (G), so 3 = B.
- 19 is adjacent to 9 (B), 23 (G), and 25 (B), so 19 = R.
- 16 is adjacent to 1 (G), 3 (B), and 19 (R). No color is left, so this case fails.

**Case 2: 7 = B.**
- 25 is adjacent to 1 (G) and 7 (B), so 25 = R.
- 23 is adjacent to 7 (B) and 25 (R), so 23 = G.
- 27 is adjacent to 0 (R), 7 (B), and 23 (G). No color is left, so this case fails.

Node 7 cannot be G because it is adjacent to 1. Both options fail, so with 1 = G there is no valid coloring. Since the choice 1 = G was WLOG (swap G and B), no 3-coloring exists.
